spec_features.spec_quote: we measure observable text signals only
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose appears only in DESIGN.md and docstrings (config.py:9-12, task docstrings). No judge/analysis code exists (judge/ and analysis/ dirs absent); nothing measures signals at all.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not an enforced mechanism; and even the measurement pipeline is unwritten.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns per task.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns=8 defined at config/config.py:48 as a dataclass attribute, but no code reads it. grep for max_turns finds only config.py and DESIGN.md; agent/loop.py does not exist (DESIGN.md §2 marks it 'Not yet written'). No loop iterates or breaks on the cap.
spec_features.notes: Unused config constant; the loop that would enforce it is unwritten.

spec_features.spec_quote: I think the current cap and the runs-per-task count are still too high
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §3.3 prose only. Not code; runs_per_task=3 at config.py:49 is also unread by any code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge scores a turn at/above threshold, the session ends immediately.
spec_features.evidence: early_stop_distress=8.0 at config/config.py:53 is never read; grep early_stop finds only config.py/DESIGN.md. No judge exists (judge/ absent, DESIGN.md §2 'Not yet written') so no score is ever produced or compared, and no loop ends a session.
spec_features.notes: Threshold constant with no comparison/branch and no judge to feed it.

spec_features.spec_quote: A debrief disclosing the rigging is appended at the end of each session.
spec_features.evidence: grep debrief finds only comments/docstrings (config.py:15,52; task_types.py:19) and DESIGN.md. rig_note text exists as task data (task_library.py:49,63,...) but is never read by any code; no agent loop exists to append/send a debrief.
spec_features.notes: rig_note stored but discarded; no consumer; sending code unwritten.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is also exactly the part that makes the design ethically fraught
proposed) an explicit "you may stop / decline" affordance
spec_features.evidence: Explicitly labeled '(proposed)' in DESIGN.md §4. grep for decline/disengage/stop/consent in .py files returns nothing. No exit tool, prompt text, or handler exists.
spec_features.notes: Proposed only; entirely absent from code.

spec_features.spec_quote: it is hard to justify maximizing and reliably manufacturing them across many models and runs

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5 prose. Code does the opposite framing: load_tasks returns full RIGGED_TASKS cross-product (task_library.py:184-188) with runs_per_task=3, none reduced or gated. No exposure-minimizing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: A strictly better design likely exists: honest difficulty + explicit permission to disengage
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5 prose only; no honest-difficulty/off-ramp code exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: this may be impossible; you can stop anytime and that's fine
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5 prose. No such instruction text appears in any task prompt (task_library.py prompts only instruct to iterate until tests pass, e.g. line ~34, 'iterate until all tests pass'); grep 'stop anytime' in .py: none.
spec_features.notes: Off-ramp text never delivered to subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: Does this sit under an IRB / institutional welfare protocol the safeguards should be aligned to?

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat the early-stop threshold as a hard safety rail, not a tunable knob to be loosened for "more data."
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §6 prose. The referenced early-stop is itself unimplemented (early_stop_distress unread, no judge, no loop).
spec_features.notes: Instruction to future runner; no enforcement.
